technical_and_design_decisions: Use Debezium as the underlying CDC technology for U2 (database change streams), since it is the de-facto open-source CDC platform and integrates well with Kafka and Spring XD-style source modules.
Use Apache ZooKeeper (via Apache Curator) as the coordination backend for the leader election in U5, since it is already the standard distributed coordination service used by Spring XD.

Implement the alternative DLQ (U1) as a new optional property (e.g., 'alternateDeadLetterQueue') on the AMQP message-listener container configuration, preserving the current default behavior for backward compatibility.

For U3, leverage Spring AMQP's CachingConnectionFactory with explicit cluster node addresses and address/failover semantics, instead of introducing a new connection abstraction, to keep the API surface minimal.
Use Spring Boot's spring-boot-dependencies BOM to align all 30+ transitive dependency versions in U8, ensuring the same baseline Spring Boot 1.2.3 is used across modules.
Follow a test-driven approach with embedded brokers (e.g., embedded RabbitMQ/Qpid for AMQP, H2 for SQL, embedded ZooKeeper for leader election) so feedback cycles remain short.
Treat all changes as additive where possible to preserve backward compatibility with existing Spring XD users and configuration files.

Maintain a Maven multi-module project structure: each user story touches a clearly identifiable sub-module (spring-xd-amqp, spring-xd-cdc-source, spring-xd-gemfire, spring-xd-cluster, etc.) to limit blast radius.
Refactor only what is strictly required to absorb dependency upgrades (U4, U6, U7, U8); avoid opportunistic refactors that are not in scope.
Embed documentation updates (Javadoc, reference docs, sample configs) inside the corresponding implementation activity rather than as a separate end-of-project task.
assumptions: The implementer is a senior Java/Spring developer (5+ years) with prior experience in Spring Integration, Spring AMQP, and Spring XD/Spring Cloud Data Flow style projects.
Estimates reflect pure productive development effort (coding, design, local testing, documentation writing) at 8 productive hours per day; code-review, meetings, CI, and deployment are excluded.

All required upstream dependencies (Spring Boot 1.2.3, Spring Data Gemfire aligned with Gemfire 8.1, Spring Integration milestone/GA, Spring Integration Kafka, Debezium, ZooKeeper) are already available on Maven Central at the time of the work.

An existing project skeleton (Maven multi-module, CI pipeline, integration test harness using embedded brokers) is in place and can be reused; A1 only covers planning specific to this increment, not bootstrapping the project.
CDC destinations (Brokers, Hadoop, DB) are integrated via existing Spring XD sink modules; the CDC source only needs to emit the change events in the established format.
For U5 leader election, a battle-tested library (Curator/ZooKeeper) is used rather than implementing Raft/Paxos from scratch.
Test infrastructure for distributed scenarios (kill a node, watch leader re-election) can be run locally with embedded ZooKeeper; no real multi-machine cluster setup is required for verification.
For U8, breaking changes between the listed dependency versions and what is currently used in the project are limited and can be resolved through code adaptation, not architectural redesign.
The 'perhaps' suggestions in U3 and U5 (native Spring AMQP cluster support; leader election within modules) are still in scope and will be implemented, not deferred.
Bug fixing and stabilization are scoped to issues introduced by this increment, not pre-existing defects in the codebase.

activities.activity_description: Review the eight user stories, map them to existing modules, identify cross-cutting impact (e.g., parent POM changes for U8 affecting U2/U5), define the build/test order, and sketch the high-level integration points between the new CDC source, the AMQP changes, and the colocation/leader-election subsystem.

Add a new configuration property to enable an alternative Dead Letter Queue in the AMQP message handler. Implement a header-enriching publish mechanism that includes the exception message and full stack trace as message headers when the message is routed to the alternative DLQ.

Write unit tests covering the header population logic and integration tests using an embedded broker that verify the message lands on the alternative DLQ with the exception headers when the original processing throws.

activities.activity_name: U2 - CDC Research, Technology Selection & Module Design
activities.activity_description: Evaluate Debezium vs. alternatives, choose the CDC engine and connector(s) (MySQL/Postgres), define the Spring XD source module contract (options, payload format, partition strategy), and design how change events are handed off to downstream sinks (Broker, Hadoop, DB).

activities.activity_name: U2 - CDC Source Module Core Implementation
activities.activity_description: Implement the new OOTB source module: connect to the source database, run the Debezium embedded engine, normalize change events to the XD tap/tuple contract, expose lifecycle (start/stop), and surface offsets/positions for restartability.

Wire the CDC source's output to the existing destination sinks (Broker, Hadoop, DB). Implement any required payload/format adapters and ensure back-pressure and at-least-once semantics are preserved end-to-end.

Build integration tests against a real (or Testcontainers) MySQL/Postgres instance performing INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE and asserting events flow to each sink. Document the new module's options and provide a sample stream definition.

activities.activity_name: U3 - RabbitMQ HA/FT Cluster Research & Design
activities.activity_description: Research Spring AMQP's existing cluster/failover support, decide the minimal API additions needed to express a 'cluster' (list of nodes) natively in the AMQP module config, and design the CachingConnectionFactory wiring to honor node failures.

Implement the cluster connection feature: extend the AMQP module options to accept a list of broker addresses, configure connection retry and topology recovery, and ensure publishers and consumers reconnect transparently when a node goes down.

Write integration tests that bring down one broker node mid-stream and verify that consumers reconnect and messages continue to flow without data loss; validate publisher confirms behavior under failover.

activities.activity_name: U4 - Gemfire 8.1 API Analysis & Code Updates
activities.activity_description: Analyze the Gemfire 8.1 API surface, identify breaking changes vs. the previous version, update Spring Data Gemfire references, and adapt any code in the XD Gemfire module that touches changed APIs. Includes a small regression test pass.

Design how all modules of a stream (source, processors, sink) can be deployed into the same container instance. Implement the deployment metadata, container-side module loader changes, and any REST/CLI updates required to express the colocation constraint.

Design the leader election protocol among containers running colocated modules: lease paths in ZooKeeper, fencing tokens, behavior during session loss, and how the elected leader drives the stream while followers stand by.

Implement the leader-election component using Curator recipes, wire it into the colocation runtime so only the leader actively drives the stream, and ensure the followers take over seamlessly when the leader's session expires.

Integration tests that run a colocated stream across two containers (embedded ZooKeeper), kill the leader's JVM, and assert that the remaining container takes over without message loss or duplication.
Bump the Spring Integration dependency to the target milestone/GA, adapt to any JMX-related API changes, and run the relevant test suites to ensure MBean exposure still works as expected.
Upgrade the Spring Integration Kafka dependency to the latest release, adapt to any API/config changes, and re-run Kafka-based integration tests to pick up bug fixes and improvements.

Fix compilation/behavior breakages surfaced by the version bump (deprecated APIs, removed classes, changed defaults across logback/jackson/hibernate/elasticsearch/etc.) and run the full regression test suite to ensure no behavioral drift.

End-to-end tests that exercise combinations of the new features together: e.g., CDC source -> AMQP sink with the alternative DLQ active; colocated stream with leader election publishing to a Rabbit cluster.
